events: Luther born at Eisleben
The son of a mining family in the county of Mansfeld.
Wittenberg founded
Frederick the Wise opens a university in his small residence town on the Elbe.
The theses on indulgences
Luther is professor of Scripture at Wittenberg. He calls for a disputation on the power of indulgences.
Melanchthon comes to Wittenberg
A Greek professor of twenty-one. He will stay for forty-two years.
The Diet of Worms
Luther refuses to recant and is hidden in the Wartburg. There he translates the New Testament.
The catechisms; Marburg
The Small and Large Catechisms appear. At Marburg Luther and Zwingli fail to agree on the Supper.
The Augsburg Confession
Read before Charles V on 25 June. It becomes the charter of the Lutheran churches.
Luther dies
At Eisleben where he was born. The Schmalkaldic War follows within months.
The Interim
The emperor imposes a settlement. Flacius goes to Magdeburg. The quarrels begin.
Jena founded
The Ernestine dukes’ answer to Wittenberg. It becomes the home of the Gnesio-Lutherans.
The Formula of Concord
Twelve articles end thirty years of controversy. The Book of Concord follows in 1580.
Gerhard’s Loci begin
The first of the nine tomes that define Lutheran orthodoxy appears at Jena.
The Thirty Years’ War
To 1648. Universities empty, and the systems keep coming.
Calov’s System
Calov was the most combative of the orthodox. His system appears at Wittenberg in twelve volumes through 1677.
Quenstedt’s Theologia
The great summary of Wittenberg orthodoxy.
Halle founded
Baier is its first prorector. The new university becomes the home of Pietism.
Hollaz’s Examen
The last of the classic Lutheran systems.

names.bio: The Wittenberg reformer whose Ninety-five Theses of 1517, against the sale of indulgences, opened the Reformation. An Augustinian friar and doctor of Scripture, he taught justification by faith alone as the heart of the gospel and defended it at Worms in 1521. His German Bible, catechisms, hymns, sermons, disputations, letters and table talk reshaped church and piety. The library holds the Weimarer Ausgabe, the critical edition of his works: the Schriften (writings and sermons) and the Tischreden (table talk).
